exposure: use of a local hemostatic gelatin sponge (GS) during cesarean section
Use of local hemostatic gelatin sponge (GS) during Cesarean section
Gelatin sponge applied vs. no gelatin sponge applied
cohort: 318 patients who underwent Cesarean section surgery
finding: While the use of a local hemostatic gelatin sponge during Cesarean section did not significantly affect the incidence of nausea, vomiting, anti-emetic drug use, febrile morbidity, or postoperative ileus, it was associated with a significantly longer time to first flatus and length of hospitalization.
mod_finding: Women who receive gelatin sponge treatment during CS should be monitored closely for the recovery of postoperative intestinal motility.
